bull_bear.body: The company's credit rating is based on its strong market position and financial performance, but high debt levels and industry competition pose risks to its credit profile.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Integrated operating model spanning quarrying, processing and distribution of granite, with a significant proportion of raw material sourced from captive quarries, supporting consistency in quality and supply
- India's largest exporter of premium quartz surfaces via wholly owned subsidiary PESL
- Access to advanced Bretonstone technology supplied by Breton SpA, Italy, including newer KREOS and Chromia technologies for premium ultra-thin and high-definition quartz slabs
- More than three decades of operational experience in granite quarrying and stone processing
- Expanding global dealer and distribution network reducing dependence on any single export market
- Broad quartz design portfolio of over 100 designs catering to varied consumer preferences
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- U.S. market / trade restriction concentration — A significant portion of the Company's product exports is directed towards the U.S. market, so financial performance remains dependent on continued access to it; any increase in tariffs, trade restrictions or other market access barriers may adversely impact operations, demand visibility and overall business performance.
- Currency exchange rate fluctuations — A substantial portion of revenue is derived from export markets, and the Company also carries foreign currency-denominated debt obligations and imports certain raw materials and capital equipment, so forex fluctuations may affect financial performance and cash flows.
- Financial risk from capex programme — PESL's capital expenditure plans include strategic investments towards capacity expansion, productivity enhancement, technology upgradation and operational efficiency improvement; any significant increase in capex beyond revenue generation levels may adversely impact the Company's financial position and cash flows.
- Production and sales risk during quarry development — The Company may be exposed to operational and financial risks during the initial development phase of its quarries, as sufficient production levels and revenue generation may take time to stabilise and fully support ongoing operational requirements.
- Operational / geological risk in quarrying — Quarrying operations are exposed to risks arising from both anticipated and unforeseen geological conditions and operational hazards.
- Quarry development / product quality consistency risk — The commissioning of multiple new quarries may create variations in quality between earlier and current production, which could potentially impact customer demand and exert pressure on product pricing.
- Environmental regulatory risk — Quarrying operations are subject to evolving environmental laws and regulatory requirements; changes in standards and stricter enforcement may increase compliance obligations, penalties for non-compliance and scrutiny of new projects through detailed environmental assessments.
- Health hazard exposure in quartz fabrication (respirable crystalline silica) — The quartz surfaces industry has seen increased acknowledgment of health hazards from respirable crystalline silica exposure for fabricators, prompting international regulators to issue safety alerts and new regulations; PESL has implemented mitigation measures including dust-suppression cutting equipment, training and health screenings.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Pokarna is engaged in natural granite quarrying, stone processing and, through its wholly owned subsidiary Pokarna Engineered Stone Limited (PESL), engineered quartz surface manufacturing marketed under the Quantra brand. The granite division follows an integrated model of quarrying, processing and distribution of granite blocks and slabs, with a significant share of raw material sourced from captive quarries, while the quartz business exports premium surfaces for residential, commercial and hospitality applications. The Company serves both domestic and international markets, with international sales concentrated in the United States, China and other select regions and a growing presence in Europe.

business.title: Competitive strengths

business.title: Quality certifications

outlook.body:
- Strengthening leadership position in engineered surfaces industry, expanding market presence and enhancing customer value
- Firm focus on innovation and quality in the quartz business, leveraging Breton's Kreos and Chromia technologies
- Continuing to explore new geographical export markets, particularly Europe, to support future growth and retain leadership position
- Exploring cut-to-size business opportunities that offer value addition and help improve margins
- Strengthening brand and expanding opportunities in the domestic market
- Operational excellence priority: improving productivity and efficiency through optimum resource utilisation, enhancing quarry productivity to reduce production costs and improve yields
- Promoting differentiated finishes and textures for outdoor granite applications to support improved realisations
- Reviving certain non-operational quarries as market conditions improve
- Market diversification, customer engagement and operational efficiencies to sustain presence across major export regions including North America and Europe
- Continued investment in advanced technologies, manufacturing excellence, sustainability, digital transformation and people development
- Product diversification and premiumization in engineered quartz via commercialization of BRETON KREOS and CHROMIA technologies for ultra-thin and high-definition slabs
- The Company follows a Board-approved Dividend Distribution Policy (per SEBI LODR Regulation 43A) that specifies the financial parameters, factors and circumstances considered in determining dividend distribution to shareholders versus retaining profits, with the stated aim of protecting investor interests through transparency; no amount was proposed for transfer to the general reserve during the year.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: PESL's capital expenditure plans include strategic investments towards capacity expansion, productivity enhancement, technology upgradation, operational efficiency improvement, and maintenance or replacement of existing facilities and equipment. The Company believes its existing capital resources and cash flows will be adequate to meet projected operational requirements, capital expenditure plans and other financial obligations, and has secured borrowings in recent years to support business expansion and operational requirements. At the quarry level, the Company continued to focus on enhancing productivity to reduce production costs and improve yields, and looks forward to reviving certain non-operational quarries as market conditions improve.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Granite Division under pressure from weak export demand, particularly from China, and increasing competition from engineered stone and alternative surface materials in key markets such as the United States and Europe
- Quartz surfaces business faced a challenging operating environment owing to geopolitical uncertainties, ongoing global conflicts, and tariff-related developments in the United States and other key international markets
- Decline in FY26 performance primarily attributable to weaker demand conditions in both granite and engineered stone businesses, driven largely by high tariffs imposed by United States authorities
- Evolving global trend: granite increasingly used in exterior applications while quartz remains the preferred choice for interior applications
- Availability of exotic granite and quartzite from Brazil, coupled with limited development of new granite quarries, leading to a gradual shift in market dynamics
- Market sentiment remained subdued during the year due to uncertain conditions arising from U.S. tariff measures, though the Company retained its customer base
